messages.author: 33e9bc7a393c10a8
messages.subject: dot_plot bin positions / breaks
parts:
Hi,

I'm starting out with ggplot2 and I'm slightly confused by the positioning of dots along the x-axis.

For example, I have a data frame containing a column AGE. The minimum recorded age is twenty for which there was only one case. The code, 

dotAge <- ggplot(dmgrph, aes(AGE))+xlab("")+ggtitle("Age")
dotAge01 <- dotAge + geom_dotplot(binwidth=1, method = "histodot")
dotAge01

produces a dotplot such that the dot relating to the observation of 20 is to the left of the 20 tickmark. As such, the plot is misleading since one might mistakenly think the smallest observation was less than 20.

Clearly the problem has to do with where the first bin starts. I.e. 19<x<=20 will plot the dot to the left of 20, while 19.5<x<=20.5 should give something more inline with what I want. Can I set the "breaks" (base graphics terminology) manually?

I have attached the data file. This is for a first year stats service course. 

Kind regards,

Stefan

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: dot_plot bin positions / breaks
parts:
You can use the 'origin' argument, which gets passed along to stat_bin. For example:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) + geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, method='histodot', origin=9)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) + geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, method='histodot', origin=9.5)
